Keep this a focused generator/validator and durable cost primitives, not the A04 service/worker or M04/M05 meeting package. No generic framework, ORM, arbitrary CLI executor, tools registry or vector index. Use strict frozen dataclasses/explicit wire parsing/SchemaError and A01 source/claim validators. Test data synthetic; do not touch private holdout inputs (none created).

1. Immutable evaluation parameters: pinned canonical expected actual model ID, prompt template content/hash/version, per-job budget/pricing version (including max cost, input bytes/output bound/call bound/timeout), validation rules version. Stable evaluation key includes these per-task parameters and actual transport model identity; config audit hash additionally includes daily limit/config values. Daily cap-only change must NOT change evaluation comparability key. Every accepted draft revision freezes source-set hash, exact parameter/evaluation/config hashes, actual model identity and usage/cost status. Reject aliases drifting to an unpinned returned model ID, missing identity/usage metadata where required, unknown versions and malformed/unknown fields. Model output JSON itself cannot assert its model identity, grant, approved/executed state, citations URL, or validation result. Actual identity/usage come from a trusted transport response, not model-authored JSON. Do not invent actual identity when absent.

2. Narrow read-only model transport: existing generic Backend.run returns text only and may wrap tool-capable CLIs, so do NOT silently adapt it. Define a small trusted transport request/response boundary accepting only bounded serialized input, fixed parameters, output bound and remaining time/cancellation. No shell commands, arbitrary tools, write credentials or source-origin instructions executed. A04 will supply/audit the concrete production adapter; injected Python test fakes are not proof of real provider isolation. No actual model call is needed in this task. Keep source excerpts/goals clearly delimited as untrusted data under a fixed instruction; do not depend on delimiters alone for validation. Mandatory trusted before-IO/current-lease/authorization checkpoint supplied by service code, invoked before each new transport call and before accepting output; no authorized=true shortcut or silent no-op default. Current per-source grant/resource/ACL binding remains A04's integration responsibility, explicitly documented, not replaced by a source hash.

3. Strict model response and validation: reuse BriefClaim and validate_claims. Bounded JSON object with explicit schema; reject unknown/missing keys, explicit null where omitted required, duplicate IDs/JSON keys, NaN/inf/bools as counts, extra prose/fences/trailing JSON, invalid source IDs, invented citation URLs, tool-call/executable command fields and approval-state fields (ordinary quoted/proposed action text remains inert data, not a reason to execute or a blanket keyword ban). Model cites only source_id; any link is resolved through trusted source metadata mapping and cannot be overridden in output. Reject URL/link escape paths in rendered fields or ensure they remain inert text for later rendering; no generated URL can become provenance. Facts, source-reported commitments and proposals remain distinct, with proposals never approved/executed. Freeze known coverage/gaps from trusted collection input, not from whatever claims arrive; partial input cannot set complete=true or output a global completeness assertion. Produce visible deterministic partial/semantic-review status. Do not pretend that source_id existence proves natural-language truth: if adding numeric/key-fact checks, compare explicit typed slots to trusted evidence, never use 'all numbers/characters appeared somewhere' as a truth test. General semantic grounding still needs real-model and human evaluation; document the limit honestly. No unsupported claim may be upgraded into a verified decision merely because schema passed.

4. Durable cost reservations in the A02-owned brief database: additive versioned forward migration, preserve ownership/application_id and readable schema interval behavior, no Monitor changes or second DB. Namespace/job/day ledger independent of config hash so config changes or restart do not erase spend. Use exact bounded integer money units (e.g. micro-USD); validate all booleans/NaN/negative/overflow inputs. Atomic conservative maximum reservation BEFORE each call checks BOTH pinned job cap across attempts and current UTC-day namespace cap; concurrent jobs/calls cannot oversubscribe. Bind reservation to actual stored job/current lease and unique logical call ID, not user-asserted namespace. Reservation state must allow at most one caller to start a logical transport call even under duplicate execution. Started/unknown reservations count against limits after crash, timeout, cancel or missing usage; unknown is not zero and no automatic refund on ambiguous outcomes. Known pre-call cancellation may release an unstarted reservation deterministically; no repeated key may produce another provider call. Settle known usage once with clear idempotency/conflict rules; contradictory repeats rejected. Actual overrun above configured reservation is recorded and stops new calls, never hidden or clamped to a fake successful cap. These are admission limits/estimates; do not claim control over provider-side billing. Store accounting may record late cost evidence without authorizing a stale draft commit; document a bounded trusted reconciliation boundary.

5. Cancellation/time budgets: honor the original persisted hard deadline, remaining task cost/call limits across retries, and explicit cancellation. Do not reset a task/day budget for each invocation, recovery, new config hash or generator object. No provider IO after checkpoint/reservation denial, cancellation or stale lease. Stop accepting output on cancellation/deadline/model mismatch/schema failure, but retain actual/unknown spend and diagnostics. Async/cooperative transport with explicit timeout contract is acceptable; do not introduce an unbounded blocking Backend.run. The A04 worker owns heartbeat/process custody and CLI kill/reap if a future CLI adapter exists; client cancellation cannot guarantee remote billing stops. Tests must distinguish cancellation requested from proven provider termination.

6. Input/output bounds apply to the WHOLE serialized model request and returned body, not only excerpts. A01 SourceSet caps total500 and M01's two provider maxima could sum1000; do not silently truncate/reinterpret these. Reject oversize input before IO; M04/M05 will reconcile provider quotas with visible coverage/versioned source limits. Empty/no usable source evidence -> clear non-ready outcome, no call. No automatic Feishu messages/outbox completion or product deployment here; A04 composes generator result with atomic store completion after current authorization.

Meaningful tests: frozen parameters/hash identity and daily-cap-only comparability; strict malformed/duplicate-key model JSON and false model ID/unknown version; invented/unknown source/URL/tool/approval fields; hostile excerpts remain data and cannot cause extra calls or override output checks; missing/partial coverage visible and cannot masquerade as complete; numeric facts if supported compare explicit evidence slots; large multibyte whole requests/output reject; current checkpoint called before IO and before accept; cancellation/timeout/stale lease cannot accept late output; no-call on cap denial; per-job cumulative retries and per-day multi-job caps with simultaneous reservations; restart preserves spend/unknown/started records; duplicate call ID at most one fake provider call; settlement duplicate/conflict/overrun; forward migration from actual A02 schema preserving jobs/leases/outbox and incompatible newer/foreign DB refusal; all A02 tests remain green. Use deterministic fakes/events and avoid long sleeps.

Report exact RED/GREEN and actual remaining integration/live-model limits. Keep code comprehensible and scope narrow.

Pin the per-job budget/profile/evaluation identity in durable accounting at first use (or validate against the stored immutable job snapshot): later invocations with a different per-job cap/profile must not silently increase the same job's quota. The model-call bound is cumulative per JOB, not per attempt, and should respect the initial+2 read-only retry maximum. A current daily-cap change may affect new admission and config audit, but cannot erase earlier job/day charges or change the per-task evaluation key by itself.

Accounting boundary cases: choose and document one UTC-day charging policy. A reservation made before midnight must not start IO after midnight under an unchecked new-day cap; safely re-reserve/revalidate the start day or deny the stale-day start. Late settlement stays attached to the original charged bucket and cannot authorize output. Trusted clocks must be sampled after DB lock acquisition, preserving A02 timing fixes. Input tokens/usage and money are exact bounded integers; conservative maximum reservation must actually cover the configured input/output/pricing bounds or explicitly prevent an under-reserved call. Recording an estimate is not a guarantee of provider billing. All current per-job budget/evaluation pins must survive new generator instances and retries.
